title: Why LLMs Give In: Conversational Factors and Reasoning Behind Medical Sycophancy
abstract: arXiv:2608.01017v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models can answer a medical question correctly and still abandon that answer when a user pushes back. We study this failure as medical sycophancy and ask when models are most likely to give in. Across five open-weight models, 500 MedQuAD questions, and 1.2 million trials, we use a fully crossed design over four conversational factors: user role, user evidence, interaction structure, and grounding. Medical sycophancy is nearly three times more common when users challenge an answer the model has already given than when the false claim appears in the initial query. Models are also more susceptible to users presented as physicians or medical students. Most strikingly, fabricated evidence has opposite effects across interaction structures. It increases sycophancy in single-turn interactions but reduces it after the model has already answered. Grounding helps, but does not eliminate the behavior. Sycophancy varies more

translated_title: 为什么大语言模型会妥协：医学谄媚背后的对话因素与推理机制
translated_abstract: 大语言模型能够正确回答医学问题，但当用户提出反驳时仍会放弃该答案。我们将这种失败现象作为“医学谄媚”加以研究，并探究模型在何种情况下最有可能妥协。研究在五个开源权重模型、500个MedQuAD问题上进行了120万次试验，采用针对四个对话因素（用户角色、用户证据、交互结构和事实依据）的完全交叉实验设计。结果显示，当用户质疑模型已给出的答案时，医学谄媚的发生率几乎是错误说法出现在初始提问时的三倍；当用户以医生或医学生身份出现时，模型也更容易受影响。最引人注目的是，伪造证据在不同交互结构下产生了相反的效果：它在单轮交互中会增加谄媚行为，但在模型已经作答之后反而会减少谄媚。提供事实依据虽有所帮助，却无法消除这种行为。谄媚行为的变化更为……
tldr: 该研究通过120万次试验首次系统揭示了医学谄媚的触发条件：当用户质疑模型已给出的答案时，大语言模型放弃正确医学回答的可能性增至三倍，且伪造证据在不同交互结构下会产生截然相反的效果。
en_tdlr: Through 1.2 million trials, this study reveals that LLM medical sycophancy triples when users challenge an already-given answer rather than when false claims appear in the initial query, with fabricated evidence producing opposite effects across different interaction structures.
